newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC said not to let in new members until 1998.
newsitem.headline: APEC said not to let in new members until 1998.

text.p: The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum will not let in new members until 1998 at the earliest, Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said on Thursday.
APEC leaders holding their summit in the Philippines on Monday will allow a three-year moratorium on new members to lapse at the end of 1996, Siazon told reporters.
But they will not admit new members immediately, despite a push by Southeast Asian nations to bring Vietnam into the APEC fold.
They will announce their criteria for new members at their next summit in Canada in 1997 and then decide which countries they will let in at the following annual meeting in Kuala Lumpur in 1998.
"It will be a two to three-year process," the foreign minister said, adding that the new members would attend their first summit in 1999.

APEC members are Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
Several nations have expressed interest in joining, including India, Pakistan, Russia, Colombia, Ecuador and Mongolia.
The Philippines and other Southeast Asian nations have expressed strong support for Vietnam to join as soon as possible.
APEC, a loose association rather than a formal trade bloc like the European Union, is committed to lowering all trade and investment barriers in the region by 2020.
